Dropbox CLI — What is it?
There are two tools:

dbxcli (Dropbox's official CLI — Go binary)

# Install on Macbrew install dbxcli# Or download from github.com/dropbox/dbxcli# Commandsdbxcli ls /onemind-codex/          # List filesdbxcli get /onemind-codex/file.md  # Download filedbxcli put local.md /onemind-codex/ # Upload filedbxcli search "credit repair"       # Search filenamesdbxcli du                           # Show space usage
Use cases for your VPS:

Install dbxcli on the DigitalOcean VPS ? agents can read/write binary files (PDFs, images) that Git doesn't track
Script selective downloads: dbxcli get /onemind-codex/_docs/some-contract.pdf
Agent pulls a specific PDF for RAG processing without syncing the whole vault
Dropbox HTTP API v2
Full REST API at api.dropboxapi.com. Key endpoints:

files/list_folder — browse directory contents
files/download — download a file
files/search — search by filename
files/upload — upload <150MB files
files/list_folder/longpoll — watch for changes (event-driven)
The longpoll endpoint is gold — your OpenClaw agent could subscribe to Dropbox change events and react to new files. —————————————————————— DigitalOcean's GenAI platform docs weren't accessible, but here's what's actually possible and more relevant to your stack:
Option A: OpenClaw's Native Search (Already Working)
Your VPS already has this running:
  • Hybrid BM25 + vector search over the codex
  • memorySearch.extraPaths ? /home/onemind/onemind-os/codex — already indexing your vault
  • OpenAI embeddings, MMR diversity reranking, temporal decay
This only searches git-tracked files (~3,601 markdown files). It does NOT search PDFs/binaries.
Option B: pgvector + PDF Processing (Best for your stack)
You already have PostgreSQL + pgvector running on your VPS (onemind-postgres). The architecture:

Pipeline:
  1. dbxcli or Dropbox API pulls PDFs from Dropbox to VPS
  2. Python script extracts text (PyPDF2, pdfplumber, or unstructured)
  3. Embed with OpenAI or local model (Nomic Embed)
  4. Store chunks + vectors in your existing pgvector database
  5. OpenClaw agents query via a custom skill
Option C: ChromaDB / Milvus Lite (Simpler, Self-Contained)
Your offline architecture doc already mentions ChromaDB. For a lightweight option:
  • MemSearch (from your research — Zilliz/memsearch) — ONNX local embeddings, no API key needed, BM25+vector
  • Mount Dropbox folder ? MemSearch watches it ? auto-indexes

My Revised Recommendation

Option A (Dropbox + Obsidian Sync) is the right move for you. Here's why:
  1. Dropbox is still correct for the long-term foundation — it gives you RAG, API, VPS access, offline folders, affordable 2TB. No other service checks all those boxes.
  2. Obsidian Sync Standard ($4/mo) solves the mobile gap cleanly — it's designed for exactly your use case (read + review + light edits on phone). Sync only markdown (618 MB fits in the 1 GB limit easily). Don't sync PDFs/images to phone.
  3. The dual-sync risk is manageable — you're one person, not a team. The conflict scenario requires editing the same file on two devices within the same ~5 second window. When it does happen, Dropbox creates a "conflicted copy" file that you can manually resolve. It won't lose data.
  4. Git remains your version control backbone — every md change is committed, pushed, and available to VPS agents.
Total cost: $16/mo for 2TB Dropbox + Obsidian Sync Standard. That gives you universal access everywhere — Mac, phone, VPS, agents, RAG, USB-portable future.
